paper.title: Algorithm 616: Hodges-Lehmann location estimator (title as in the Netlib/CALGO index; not verified against the paper)

code.commit: netlib TOMS archive 616.gz, sha256 d81e3935449161431649327e1fa3c729db01af4475ebf1c7e9f3e881d1649c99 (fetched 2026-11-26 19:34Z). The file is the Fortran source (lines 1-354, MAIN, RAN, RANG, HLQEST, HSORT), then the stdin data for the second test (lines 355-365), then the printed output of the run (lines 366-441).
code.note: The file does not compile as shipped: lines 355-441 are data and printed output, not Fortran. The source is lines 1-354 and the stdin is lines 355-365 (N=6..N=7 tie data, then N=0 to stop). Rerun must cut these line ranges (a source patch, as with 677), compile with a Fortran compiler (gfortran) and feed the stdin. RAN and RANG are integer LCGs (Lewis-Goodman-Miller, Schrage), so the random input is deterministic given seed 434977; no 32-bit overflow occurs in the arithmetic (checked by reading). Single precision REAL is used throughout.

claim.location: The archive's printed run output (616.gz lines 366-441), FIRST TEST OF HLQEST USING RANDOM INPUT: the line ' N=  9 REP  3   H-L ESTIMATOR VIA HLQEST=     .545388'.
claim.metric: The Hodges-Lehmann estimate printed by the driver for N=9, repetition 3, via HLQEST (median of the N(N+1)/2 Walsh averages of the random sample, RANG seed 434977), printed F12.6, compared with the shipped value 0.545388. The same printed line also gives the sorting value .545388 for the same sample; the claim is the HLQEST line.
claim.paper_value: Not used: the paper (ACM DL) was not read and no numeric value of the paper was located. The claim rests on the archive's printed run output, as artifact-reference.

values.name: H-L estimator via HLQEST, N=9 rep 3, first test (random input)

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The shipped value is printed with F12.6, so 1e-6 is one unit in the sixth decimal (the last printed digit). A larger difference is a finding to diagnose (compiler, single-precision arithmetic, the generator), not a licence to loosen it. Any value that differs at the sixth decimal is a finding, not a pass.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 minute (the first test is 27 small random samples, N<=9).
cost.data_size: None: the sample is generated by the program's own generator; the second-test data are in the file (lines 355-365).
cost.data_licence: Netlib CALGO (ACM) code under the ACM licence; the rerun should record the licence text from the archive.

why: Location estimator whose printed run output comes from the same code, computed with a deterministic integer generator; the HLQEST value needs the Walsh-average median computed by the algorithm, not a closed form, and the same run prints an independent sorting value for the same sample, so a mismatch is visible.
